newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan household spending gradually recovering - govt.
newsitem.headline: Japan household spending gradually recovering - govt.

text.p: Household spending in Japan is gradually recovering, the Management and Coordination Agency said on Thursday.
Household spending fell 1.0 percent in real terms in April due to a fall-off in consumer spending after a sales tax increase in April, an agency official told reporters.
The sales tax was lifted to five percent from three percent on April 1.

Spending on food, furniture, household goods and clothing fell in April from March, but the decline was roughly equivalent to the rise in spending in March when consumers rushed to make purchases ahead of the tax increase, the official said.

"There is no change in the trend of a gradual recovery," the official said, although he added that it was important to watch the data for May, because when the sales tax was first introduced in 1989 the fall-off in consumer spending was greater in May than in April.
